updates.title: GitHub made local sandboxing broadly available across Copilot coding agents
updates.whatChanged: GitHub made local sandboxing generally available at no extra cost in Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, and VS Code sessions using Agent Host. It constrains agent-run commands' access to files, networks, and credentials, and enterprise-managed settings can require and configure sandboxing.
updates.whyCare: Coding agents can execute commands with the developer's privileges, so restricting their filesystem, network, and credential access is a practical adoption control. A first-party option across common Copilot surfaces can reduce reliance on separately assembled local restrictions.
updates.before: Without local sandboxing, Copilot CLI commands ran with the user's access; organizations wanting local execution limits had to rely on other system controls or use a separate cloud execution environment.
updates.after: Organizations can enable local OS-level sandboxing across several Copilot coding surfaces and enforce policy centrally, while keeping work on the developer's machine.
updates.learn: Treat sandboxing as a boundary to configure and validate, not as proof that agent actions are safe. Test filesystem, network, credential, MCP/LSP, and bypass policies on each supported OS; local sandboxing is lighter-weight than a separate VM or container, while GitHub's cloud sandbox provides an isolated remote environment with usage-based billing.

sources.name: GitHub Changelog - GitHub Copilot weekly releases, October 5
GitHub Docs - About cloud and local sandboxes for GitHub Copilot

updates.architectureImplication: Evaluate the feature against locally managed OS restrictions and custom container/VM-based development environments. Validate its OS-specific enforcement, managed-policy behavior, and exceptions against the enterprise threat model; prefer the cloud sandbox or stronger isolation where local process-level controls are insufficient, accounting for its separate usage-based cost.
